newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia in open skies deal with U.S. around June.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia in open skies deal with U.S. around June.

text.p: Malaysia expects to sign an "open skies" treaty liberalising air travel with the United States around June, Transport Minister Ling Liong Sik said on Wednesday.

He told reporters that the agreement is to be signed soon after the June 22 to 24 transport ministers meeting of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) in Victoria, Canada. He did not give a more specific date.
Ling said differences between the two countries on the agreement have been pared down to "a few words".
"We're down to just a few words, 90 over percent" have been agreed upon, he said.
The minister last month said the agreement will provide for unlimited landings and intermediate points to continue flights to other countries by carriers from the two countries.
Malaysia was also willing to sign open skies agreements with other nations if they were based on "reciprocity and balance of opportunities", Ling said.
Malaysian Airline System Bhd (MAS) currently flies six times a week to Los Angeles.
MAS chairman Tajudin Ramli said last month that the agreement would benefit the airline and improve the company's profits.
